title: Fixed-scalar encoding after a coefficient isomorphism
statement: Let A be a topological commutative ring, R a condensed commutative ring, and e:R ≅ underline A_cont an isomorphism of ring objects. On any scheme T, define F_T to be termwise restriction along the inverse pulled-back coefficient isomorphism, followed by the fixed-scalar derived functor of a normalized Encoding A T. This functor is an equivalence: restriction along the inverse ring isomorphism is an exact equivalence, and so is the normalized encoding. No choice of unproved data enters F_T.

source.place: Coefficient transport and clauses (2)--(3), canonical-map identifications.

proof.text: Pull the inverse ring isomorphism back from the profinite point. Restriction of scalars is inverse to restriction along its inverse; both preserve the underlying abelian sheaf and are exact. Apply the exact-functor derived construction and compose with Encoding.fixedDerived. The two functors are equivalences, hence so is their composite.
